item.description: The strong first-round performance of right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has raised questions over the future of Brazil’s policy towards Palestine, as President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva heads into a closely contested run-off. Bolsonaro secured around 47 per cent of the vote, compared with roughly 45 per cent for Lula, outperforming several pre-election polls and reinforcing broader gains by right-wing forces in congressional and regional races. For supporters of Palestine, the result has made Brazil’s election about more than domestic politics. Under Lula, Brazil has remained a strong supporter of Palestinian statehood and self-determination, while openly criticising Israeli settlement expansion and the war in Gaza. Queuing for water and phone charging: What survival looks like in Gaza
item.description:
Queuing for water and phone charging: What survival looks like in Gaza

As Israel's genocide enters its fourth year, daily life for Palestinians has been reduced to finding food and water while coping with loss and displacement

Nearly two years after Raja al-Shawish's husband went missing at an Israeli checkpoint, she says she no longer feels like a woman.

Since his disappearance, she has had to bear the responsibility of raising her children alone, from the moment she wakes up, until the time she goes to sleep.

The routines that once gave her a sense of herself have been replaced by the daily demands of survival, leaving little room for the life she once knew or the woman she once was.

"My husband was with me during the first year of the genocide, and although it was harsh, he would carry the burden with me and make it feel less devastating," Raja told Middle East Eye from an Unrwa classroom in western Gaza City that has been her home for around two years.

"Since he disappeared, and during the starvation, I have sold all my gold - except for one piece - to feed our children. I kept the last piece for when he returns. I will sell it then and use the money to celebrate."

Read more: Queuing for water and phone charging: What survival looks like in Gaza

item.title: Hamas rejects Guterres’s 7th October statement, accuses him of adopting Israeli narrative
item.description: Hamas on Tuesday rejected a statement by UN Secretary-General António Guterres marking the anniversary of the 7th October 2023 attack, accusing him of adopting Israel’s account of events and disregarding the broader context of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. In a statement, Hamas said Guterres’s remarks contained what it described as “fallacies proven false” and disregarded established facts, calling on the UN chief to retract what the group termed “fabrications.” Hamas also criticised what it described as Guterres’s “softened language” in addressing Israel’s military campaign in Gaza and its impact on the Palestinian population. The statement came in response to remarks by Guterres marking the 7th October anniversary, in which he described the Palestinian-led attack on Israel as “horrific and large-scale terrorism.” […]

item.title: Al-Awda complex in Nuseirat suspends health services except emergency care
item.description: The Al-Awda Health and Community Complex in Nuseirat announced on Tuesday the temporary suspension of all health and medical services except reception and emergency care due to persistent problems with its electricity generators. In a brief statement, the complex said the suspension would take effect at 8:00 p.m., after repeated generator failures made it impossible to operate medical departments and services effectively. The complex said the decision was taken in coordination with Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital and the American Hospital in Deir al-Balah. Health services will remain suspended until the generator problems are resolved and the units are operational again, the complex said, citing the need to ensure patient safety and continuity of medical care. item.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say foreign warships have retreated from the Gulf
item.description:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say foreign warships have retreated from the Gulf

Submitted by MEE staff on Wed, 10/07/2026 - 11:14
Brigadier-General Yadollah Javani said foreign military vessels were now located more than a 1,000km from Iran's shores
Members of Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps march during a military parade in Iranian capital, Tehran, in 2018 (AFP)
Off

An Iranian commander says the Revolutionary Guard’s military capabilities have forced foreign naval forces to keep their distance from Iran, according to state news agency IRNA.

Brigadier-General Yadollah Javani, deputy commander of the IRGC’s political bureau, attributed the shift in the Gulf and Sea of Oman to the force’s missiles, drones and naval strength.

“Previously, dozens of foreign warships and vessels roamed the Gulf,” he said.

“Today, the enemy’s fleet has moved more than 1,000km away from our territorial waters and does not dare approach.”

Javani said “collective security of Islamic countries and the complete withdrawal of the aggressors” would determine the region’s future.

Since the war started in February, Iran has established itself as the dominant military force over the Strait of Hormuz, which serves as the choke point for the rest of the Gulf region, which was traditionally known as the Persian Gulf but has been called the Arabian Gulf by Arab states in recent decades.

The region is crucial for world energy exports. Before the war, the strait carried roughly 20 million barrels per day (bpd) – a fifth of global daily oil consumption – with an estimated 10 to 14 percent of global supply remaining inaccessible six months on.

Iranian press review: Tehran says it will no longer wait to be attacked
Read More »

But shipments have almost returned to pre-war levels, thanks to backroom deals between Gulf states and Iran, and Tehran's own exports.

On Monday, US Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said that 17 million barrels of oil transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday.

Wright added that this marked the highest level of crude oil to pass through the waterway since the war on Iran disrupted shipping.

Nevertheless, securing control of the strait and negating Iran's influence on supply remains a key US strategic goal.

On Sunday, AP reported US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth saying the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz is “ironclad” and that US President Donald Trump has “all the options he needs on the table” if Iran continues to “play games”.

“Iran wants to play games with things like the Strait of Hormuz. They don’t control it, we do,” Hegseth told reporters.

The strike in southern Gaza also wounded people, although the number remains unclear.

item.title: Israeli attacks kill Gaza rescue worker, boy and another Palestinian
item.description:
Israeli attacks kill Gaza rescue worker, boy and another Palestinian

Israeli forces have killed three Palestinians in Gaza as the territory marks three years of Israel’s genocidal war.

One attack killed a Civil Defence worker trying to rescue wounded people at a camp for displaced Palestinians near Kamal Adwan Hospital.

In southern Gaza, Israeli gunfire killed a boy east of Khan Younis, where troops continued firing heavy machine guns. A drone attack killed another person in the city.

The killings come on the third anniversary of the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023. Since then, Israeli forces have killed at least 74,000 Palestinians in Gaza, including thousands of children.
